parts.problem_md: What would cause an outward shift of a country’s production possibility curve (PPC)?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as any increase in the quantity or quality of a country’s factors of production will shift the PPC outwards

- A is incorrect as a fall in unemployment reduces the inefficiency of labour which moves a country from inside its curve towards the curve (it does not move the curve)
- B is incorrect as a PPC reveals no information on income taxes
- D is incorrect as a reduction in expenditure may shift the PPC inwards over time as the skills in a country decrease

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: a fall in unemployment

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: an increase in the rate of income tax

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: an increase in the labour force

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: a reduction in expenditure on education

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows two production possibility curves.

![Graph showing the production possibility frontiers (PPF) of capital goods and consumer goods, with points X and Y indicating different production levels.](assets/001-graph-showing-the-production-possibility-frontie.png)

Which statement about the movement from point X to point Y is correct?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as the country has managed to increase output of consumer goods without losing output of capital goods

- A is incorrect as a PPC is about the location of resources - and not the level of demand
- B is incorrect as the opportunity cost of producing consumer goods has fallen as more can be produced without losing any capital goods (Y as opposed to X)
- D is incorrect as the curve has shifted outwards

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Demand for consumer goods has risen.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: The opportunity cost for producing consumer goods has risen.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: There has been an increase in productivity in consumer goods production.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: There has been an inward shift in the production possibility curve.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a production possibility curve (PPC) for an economy that produces both capital goods and consumer goods. At which point will the economy show the highest potential for sustained long run economic growth?

![qp-june-2019v2-paper-1-cie-economics-igcse-q2](assets/002-qp-june-2019v2-paper-1-cie-economics-igcse-q2.png)
parts.solution_md:
**B is the correct answer **as the country is using its resources efficiently (on the curve) and capital goods are required in order to produce consumer goods both for domestic and foreign consumption leading to long term growth

- A is incorrect as this economy is not using its resources efficiently (inside the curve)
- C is incorrect as point B offers a higher level of production of consumer goods than point C
- D is incorrect as point B offers a higher level of production of consumer goods than point D

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a production possibility curve (PPC) for a country. The country moved from position X to position Y on the PPC.

![Graph showing a production possibilities frontier curve. The x-axis represents consumer goods, and the y-axis represents capital goods. Points X and Y are on the curve.](assets/003-graph-showing-a-production-possibilities-frontie.png)

What is the **most** likely reason for this change?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as an increase living standards usually raises incomes which leads to an increase in demand for consumer goods

- A is incorrect as an increase in technology on the production side usually leads to an increase in capital goods
- B is incorrect as the discovery of new economic resources would shift the entire PPC outwards
- D is incorrect as an increase in long-term economic growth is shown by a movement outwards of the entire PPC

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Firms have decided to increase investment in technology.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: New economic resources have been discovered in the country.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The government has brought about an increase in living standards.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: The government has encouraged long-term economic growth.

parts.problem_md: A production possibility curve shows all of the following except?
parts.solution_md:
- **B is the correct answer** as a PPC provides no information on the level of government intervention

  - A is incorrect as the idea of opportunity cost is firmly embedded into the model - by producing more of one good, some of the other good has to be sacrificed
  - C is incorrect as the potential output is represented by any point on the PPC
  - D is incorrect as the level of efficiency can be determined by observing if the economy is producing on the PPC (efficient) or inside of it (inefficient)

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: The opportunity cost of producing two goods

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: The level of government control

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The potential output of an economy using all available resources

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: The level of efficiency in the economy

What would be the opportunity cost of moving from point X to produce only consumer goods?
parts.solution_md:

- A is incorrect as consumer goods are increasing, not decreasing
- C is incorrect as capital good production is currently 70 units, not 100 units
- D is incorrect as 180 units of capital goods is the current level of production

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a production possibility curve (PPC).

![june-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q2](assets/005-june-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q2.png)

What would cause the curve to shift inwards?
parts.solution_md:
**A is the correct answer **as a natural disaster will damage the factors of production and the country will have fewer resources available from which to generate their output

- B is incorrect as the discovery of new resources will shift the curve outwards
- C is incorrect as when the workers gain new skills it will shift the curve outwards
- D is incorrect as the introduction of new technology will improve efficiency and will shift the curve outwards

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: A natural disaster such as an earthquake

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: More resources are discovered within the country

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The workers in the country gain new skills and become more productive

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: New technology increases the efficient use of resources

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a production possibility curve (PPC).

![june-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q2](assets/005-june-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q2.png)

Why is the curve usually drawn like this?
parts.solution_md:
**B is the correct answer** as the concave curve shows that there is increasing opportunity cost as factors of production are reallocated from one good to another e.g. some units of labour will initially be able to switch over easily, but as more and more are switched the economy will encounter labour that struggles to adapt and make the change

- A is incorrect as a PPC does not provide information on international trade
- C is incorrect as resources are not unlimited in supply - hence the PPC which demonstrates finite supply
- D is incorrect as unemployed resources are indicated by any point inside the curve

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: International free trade exists.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Opportunity cost changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Resources are unlimited in supply.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Some resources will be unemployed.

parts.problem_md:
Using all available resources an economy produces different combinations of two types of good, clothes and food, shown on the production possibility curve (PPC) diagram.

![screen-shot-2023-07-31-at-10-13-52-am](assets/006-screen-shot-2023-07-31-at-10-13-52-am.png)

What does the PPC indicate?
parts.solution_md:
**B is the correct answer** as any increase in clothes output has to decrease food output

- A is incorrect as any point on the PPC represents fully efficient production
- C is incorrect as the best situation will depend on a range of factors not shown by a PPC
- D is incorrect as this information cannot be deduced from a PPC

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: It is more efficient to produce more of clothes than food.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: It is only possible to increase the output of clothes by reducing the output of food.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The best situation is to produce equal units of clothes and food.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: The cost of producing a unit of clothes is always higher than the cost of producing a unit of food.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a country’s production possibility curve (PPC).

![nov-2018-v2qp-p1-cie-eco-q3](assets/007-nov-2018-v2qp-p1-cie-eco-q3.png)

Which statement is correct?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as the movement of production from point Y to Z diverts the allocation of resources from capital to consumer goods

- A is incorrect as any point on the curve is considered efficient
- B is incorrect as a movement from X to Z does not represent the discovery of new resources but a more efficient use of existing resources
- D is incorrect as any point on the curve is considered efficient

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: A movement from X to Y shows a decrease in efficiency in the economy.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: A movement from X to Z shows a discovery of new resources in the economy.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: A movement from Y to Z shows resources are being diverted from capital goods to consumer goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: A movement from Z to Y shows an increase in efficiency in the economy.

parts.problem_md:
Countries X and Y have identical resources. The diagram shows their production possibility curves.

![nov-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q2](assets/008-nov-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q2.png)

What can be concluded from the diagram?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as country Y is producing more of both goods than country X, even though they both have the same resources (Y is more efficient)

- A is incorrect as a PPC does not show the cost of production, but rather the opportunity cost
- B is incorrect as no unemployment of resources is evident in the diagram
- D is incorrect as a PPC does not provide information on price levels

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: X can produce food and drink more cheaply than Y.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: X experiences higher unemployment than Y.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Y can produce food and drink more efficiently than X.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Y has higher retail prices than X.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the production possibility curve (PPC) for an economy.

![nov-2018-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q3](assets/009-nov-2018-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q3.png)

What will happen to the opportunity cost of producing more units of consumer goods in terms of capital goods as the economy moves down its PPC from point X to point Z?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as the concave curve shows that there is increasing opportunity cost as factors of production are reallocated from X to Y to Z e.g. some units of labour will initially be able to switch over easily, but as more and more are switched the economy will encounter labour that struggles to adapt and make the change, meaning the opportunity cost is higher

- A is incorrect as it is increasing
- B is incorrect as it is continually increasing as production moves towards consumer goods
- D is incorrect as the opportunity cost initially increases at a lower rate up to point  Y and then continues to increase at an increasing rate - it does not decrease

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: It will decrease continuously from point X to point Z.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: It will decrease up to point Y and then increase towards point Z.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: It will increase continuously from point X to point Z.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: It will increase up to point Y and then decrease towards point Z.

parts.problem_md:
Country X provides computers to help teachers in the classroom.

How would this technology increase the economic potential of country X?
parts.solution_md:
**A is the correct answer** as a computer is a capital good that will improve the quality of the education and skills in the economy ultimately causing the PPC to shift outwards

- B is incorrect as it has no impact on land
- C is incorrect as teachers are still required to use and operate the computers
- D is incorrect as it may lead to fewer teachers being required - or have no impact on the number of teachers

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: It improves the quality of human resources.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: It reduces the amount of land required for education.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: It removes the need for teachers.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: It requires more teachers to do the same work.

The diagram shows the production possibility curve (PPC) of a country producing at point T.

![qp-0455-m20qp-12-q2](assets/010-qp-0455-m20qp-12-q2.png)

The country has an ageing population and decides to allocate more resources to the production of health services. Which movement shows this change in resource allocation?
parts.solution_md:
**C is the correct answer** as more health service means less non-health services provided with an efficient allocation of resources

- A is incorrect moving from T to S creates inefficiencies A point inside the PPC) and produces more non-health services and fewer health benefits
- B is incorrect as U is unattainable
- D is incorrect as fewer health services are generated by this movement and more non-health services
